 The Saint Mary’s Gaels (3-1) hope to extend a three-game home winning streak when they host the Portland State Vikings (2-2) on November 16, 2026.
 On Friday, in its most recent game, Saint Mary’s (CA) beat UIC 84-61. With 20 points, Darius Bivins was its high scorer. In its previous game, Portland State defeated San Francisco on Saturday, 84-68. Yaroslav Nikonov scored a team-high 27 points (and added seven assists and six boards).
 When is Saint Mary’s (CA) vs. Portland State and when does it start?
 This contest between the Gaels and Vikings will take place on Monday, November 16, 2026. You can expect the opening tip at 10 p.m. ET.
 Where to Watch Saint Mary’s (CA) vs. Portland State
 The Gaels and Vikings will hit the court at University Credit Union Pavilion for this matchup on Nov. 16, and if you’d like to see the event live, get your tickets now from Vivid Seats ! 
 What channel is the game on?
 You can catch this game live on ESPN+ .

 Saint Mary’s Gaels vs. Portland State Vikings Game Preview
 Saint Mary’s (CA) Stats, Odds & Insights (2025-26)
 On offense, Saint Mary’s (CA) was the 138th-ranked team in the nation (77.3 points per game) last year. On defense, it was seventh-best (64.5 points conceded per game).
 Last year, the Gaels scored 7.0 more points per game (77.3) than the Vikings allowed (70.3).
 Last season, Saint Mary’s (CA) was 138th in the country in 3-point makes (8.2 per game) and eighth-best in 3-point percentage (39.0%).
 The Gaels put up 83.7 points per game in home games last season, compared to 72.3 points per game in away games, a difference of 11.4 points per contest.
 Portland State Stats, Odds & Insights (2025-26)
 Last year Portland State put up 76.6 points per game (153rd-ranked in college basketball) and ceded 70.3 points per contest (74th-ranked).
 The Vikings put up an average of 76.6 points per game last year, 12.1 more points than the 64.5 the Gaels gave up.
 Portland State was 283rd in the nation with 6.7 treys per game last season. Meanwhile, it ranked 268th with a 32.4% shooting percentage from three-point land.
 At home, the Vikings scored 79.7 points per game last season, 6.2 more than they averaged away (73.5).
